question: What is u in the equation s = ut + 1/2 at², which represents the position-time relation?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Initial velocity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the equation **s = ut + 1/2 at²**, **u** stands for the **initial velocity** of the object.
 
• This equation is one of the fundamental equations of motion in classical mechanics, often referred to as the **second equation of motion**.
 
• The term **s** represents the **displacement** or position change of the object.
 
• The term **t** represents the **time** duration over which the motion occurs.
 
• The term **a** stands for the **acceleration** of the object.
 
• The equation combines **initial velocity (u)**, **acceleration (a)**, and **time (t)** to determine the **displacement (s)**.
 
• This equation is derived from the basic principles of **Newtonian mechanics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uniform acceleration**__

 __
 
• **Uniform acceleration** refers to a constant rate of change in velocity.
 
• In equations of motion, **acceleration (a)** is often assumed to be uniform.
 
 
 
• **Speed of the object**__
 __
 
• **Speed** is a scalar quantity representing how fast an object is moving.
 
• Speed does not include direction, unlike velocity, which is a vector quantity.
 
 
 
• **Change in momentum**__
 
 
• **Momentum** is the product of the mass and velocity of an object.
 
• The change in momentum is often described by the impulse-momentum theorem.
